title: Fundamental Limits of Prescribed-Time Regulation: Gain Budgets, Accuracy Frontiers, and Arrival Costs
summary: Prescribed-time controllers drive the state to the origin at a time $T$ chosen in advance, with gains that grow without bound as $t$ approaches $T$. This paper shows the growth is a necessity and computes the exact price of avoiding it. The starting point is a simple estimate: any trajectory with $\|\dot z(t)\|\le L(t)\|z(t)\|$ satisfies $\|z(t)\|\ge\|z(0)\|e^{-\int_0^t L}$.
